name: Starter
audience: Everyone. Install this first, in every repo you work in.

items.why: Always-on rails: the agent asks before anything destructive, touches prod, or posts on your behalf.
A guided tour of any repo, so you know what it does and how to run it before you change it.
Every new file the agent creates states its purpose, owner, inputs, outputs and ticket, so your work is easy to follow from day one.
A paste-ready daily standup from your commits, specs and Jira, in under a minute.
Flags docs your changes made stale, and writes plain-English release notes and a Teams post after a merge.

addons.why: Turn it on when you're new to a codebase or to SQL and Python: it explains every change it makes.

name: Intermediate
tagline: Tools for more control, recommended for developers
audience: Once you're comfortable in Kiro and own tickets end to end.

items.why: Catches fan-out joins, NULL traps and date bugs before wrong numbers ship, on demand and on every save.
Kiro remembers your projects, conventions and decisions across sessions, so you stop re-explaining the same things.

addons.why: Useful when you pick up an unfamiliar repo: it explains every change it makes.

name: Advanced
tagline: The full toolkit for leads and power users.
audience: For people who own repos, review others' work, or keep shared metrics consistent across the team.

items.why: Team templates for commits, PRs, Jira, Teams and Confluence. Standup, Handoff and Changelog write in these formats.
Keeps a growing steering setup healthy: conflicts, always-on bloat, stale rules and broken hooks.
Hand over in-flight work cleanly before PTO or a reassignment, with nothing left only on your machine.
Finds every version of a metric across repos, Databricks, Confluence and Excel, and shows where they disagree.
Clears out dead files safely, with a 14-day holding period that catches anything still in use.
